set.summary: The Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee advanced S. 4753, the Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024, by 15-4; Sens. Sanders, Wyden, Hirono and Hawley voted no. Chairman Joe Manchin and ranking member John Barrasso had released it on July 22 and introduced it July 23. It never received a floor vote and died with the 118th Congress. House Republicans rejected it, in part over provisions easing large power lines, and co-ops and public power providers lobbied against wider FERC jurisdiction.

set.summary: Sens. Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich released the 417-page bill at a press conference. It sets a 150-day limit for NEPA claims, bars agencies from revoking issued permits except in listed cases (Sec. 1401), and requires data centers to pay their transmission costs. Wind and solar 'regular order' terms remain under negotiation with the White House, with amendment work in parallel and a vote aimed for after the Senate returns in November. In the House, Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman said most Democrats would not support the bill as written, and Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie had not endorsed it.

set.significance: FERC chose regional tariff changes over one national rule. The Senate bill would set a national cost rule by statute.
set.summary: In place of a single national rule, FERC voted unanimously on June 18, 2026 to issue Section 206 show cause orders to PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE and NYISO, preliminarily finding their tariffs may be unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear large-load and co-location provisions. Responses were due in 60 days, with generation-adequacy reports due in 30 days; DOE had asked for final action on its October 2025 proposal by April 30. The vote was 5-0. The orders cover five areas: study rules, safeguards against cost shifts, co-location, flexible service and generation near load.
